info.desc: "Station to Station" is the tenth studio album by English musician David Bowie, released by record label RCA in 1976. Commonly regarded as one of his most significant works, "Station to Station" is also notable as the vehicle for Bowie's last great 'character', The Thin White Duke. The album was recorded after he completed shooting Nicolas Roeg's "The Man Who Fell to Earth", and the cover featured a still from the movie. During the sessions Bowie was heavily dependent on drugs, especially cocaine, and recalls almost nothing of the production. Musically, "Station to Station" was a transitional album for Bowie, .

podcast.body: A funk-infused album that charted better in the US than in the UK. It reached number 3 on the Billboard album chart in the US, which was his highest charting LP in America until "The Next Day" (2013). "And the funk-infused station to station album charted a bit better in the US as well."

podcast.body: Anchored by the hit "Golden Years," this album, released in 1976, shot to number three on the Billboard LP's chart in just three weeks, holding the benchmark as Bowie's highest charting LP for the next four decades. Despite the slickness of its single, the album's lyrics reflected Bowie's cocaine-fueled paranoia, and its cover was a still from 'The Man Who Fell to Earth', introducing his gaunt "Thin White Duke" character. "Golden Years, a number 10 hit in early 76, anchored the album Station to Station, arguably the 70s Imperial Peak for David Boey."

podcast.body: Bowie admitted to having no memory of making this album due to severe cocaine use from late 1975 through to late 1976. Despite yielding only one major hit ("Golden Years"), it is now considered one of his most important albums, having been positively re-evaluated over the years, and it hinted at his musical direction for the latter half of the 70s. "a record that Bowie had no memory of making because by his own admission, he was so coked out during that entire period from late 1975 through to sometime in late 1976 that he doesn't remember a thing."

podcast.body: Bowie had absolutely no memory of recording this album in 1976, a period during which he was heavily addicted to cocaine and alcohol, leading to extreme paranoia and a significant decline in his physical and mental health. "Bowie had no memory at all of recording the station to station album in 1976."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album marks a period where David Bowie's personal life was completely out of control, characterized by extreme eccentricities, madness, and obsessive paranoias. Bowie himself reportedly could not recall composing, recording, or even touring for this album, indicating his severe state at the time. "Ese famoso disco que David Bowie nunca recordó ni haber compuesto ni haber grabado ni recuerda prácticamente nada de él, ni siquiera recuerda la gira de Station Tolstoyson."

podcast.body: This album, released in January 1976, achieved both critical acclaim and commercial success. However, at the time of its release, Bowie was unable to enjoy this triumph due to severe drug addiction affecting his mental health. "David Bowie saca el disco Station to Station, el cual es un éxito tanto de crítica como de eventa, pero hoy el es incapaz de saborear el éxito."
